state: The requested investigation concerns two implemented values subsystems inside /packages/: exact numeric behavior plus typed wire and schema admission. This is not a compiler port; /compiler is already Rust and its edits are excluded. Integration may adjust packages/values façade/build and package delivery loaders. Behavioral compatibility is the acceptance bar. Decimal representation retains authored coefficient and fractional scale, with at most38 coefficient digits and scale0 through18; trailing coefficient zeros count. Scale alignment and exact multiplication require wider intermediates than i128, division keeps the smallest terminating scale or rounds repeating results half-even at18, and aggregates validate only the complete sum. Some exposed JS helpers legally receive unlimited-size BigInts and narrow only their result. Direct wasm-bindgen integer parameters wrap values outside their width. A signed256-bit work type covers valid bounded Decimal binary calculations but cannot by itself preserve all arbitrary input helper behavior. Available choices are num-bigint arbitrary integers, bnum bounded wide integers with a compatibility route, or a bigdecimal wrapper that enforces Can rules. rust_decimal's96-bit representation is too narrow. Current TS test suites and a committed conformance corpus exist; no Rust/Wasm size or throughput experiments have been performed. Validation is more than shape checking: create-time defaults and trim, partial-update omission symbols, null distinction, complete array/union branches, closed fields, recursively required mutation-ref versions, refusal to serialize secrets and stable violation order. The input API is JS unknown, including undefined and text with isolated UTF16 surrogate units; blindly using UTF8 String or JSON can alter it. Locale, zones and WHATWG URL checks should stay at the host boundary initially. Registered schemas may become ordered typed plans at initialization, retaining parsing only for unknown external type strings; this works with existing descriptors and requires no new compiler output. Proposed deployment uses the existing synchronous TS public names with one pure Rust core and a common Wasm binary, deferring optional native addons and optimization until parity and benchmarks.

arithmetic_backend.instructions: Select the most defensible initial numeric implementation for exact package parity, judging engineering effort, semantic auditability, dependency burden and an eventual optimized path equally for each choice; runtime advantage is unknown.

criteria.bigint_first: First reproduce the Can algorithms using num-bigint for coefficients, operands and temporaries. Arbitrary JS helper inputs are represented losslessly. Once conformance matches, prove bounded fast paths and benchmark them. Downsides are allocating arithmetic, Wasm size and a possible second implementation pass.
criteria.fixed_first: Begin with i128 storage and bnum signed256-bit temporary arithmetic for validated values, retaining a separate unlimited-integer adapter/path for old helpers. Establish all intermediate and collection-length bounds before shipping. This could save allocations but demands extra proof and compatibility machinery immediately.
criteria.decimal_wrapper: Build on bigdecimal's arbitrary decimal operations, with a Can layer enforcing preserved scale,38-digit bounds,18 fractional places, half-even rules and exact error behavior. This may reduce arithmetic code, at the price of checking and overriding its context-dependent precision and formatting semantics.

validator_backend.instructions: Choose the least complicated packages-only validator architecture that retains the full observed Can behavior and can skip repeated type parsing for schema types registered at startup.

criteria.can_interpreter: Turn today's schema descriptors into a registered ordered Rust plan once and implement Can-specific validation over its resolved nodes. Parse external type IDs only in a compatibility entry and keep host checks in adapters. This owns a custom traversal but keeps value building, omission and diagnostic order explicit.
criteria.json_schema: Use a Rust JSON Schema engine as the base, adding Can format/keyword extensions, default/update transformations, value construction and ordered-error mapping. Reusable schema infrastructure and interoperability are strengths; extra dependencies and semantic translation are the costs.
criteria.hybrid: Leave the schema interpreter and diagnostic collector in JS and introduce Rust only behind exact leaf codecs, scalar checks and arithmetic. Existing high-level behavior is easier to retain, while ownership is divided and host crossings could dominate nested validation.
